content:
I’ve experienced multi-minute load times regularly for group DMs on the iOS app. Today I tried to load a new 4-person group DM with a single message in it and gave up after 10 minutes. :) The group DM in question loads instantly on the macOS app.

Have others experienced this as well? I feel I recall seeing it mentioned somewhere, but can’t find it.
I just tried loading a few of my ≥4-person group DMs in this instance on iOS and didn't have any issues (granted all except one had < 20 messages total).

We're running a big migration right now which touches every DM and group-DM. However, the mobile and desntop clients use the same API, so there shouldn't be any variation there -- and 10 minutes is far more impact than we're expecting (which is that some queries may take ~1s).
We had a bad latency spike around 2026-04-09T12:20:00-04:00, if that lines up with when you were having issues.
But we've since addressed it.
Hmm, while the 10+ minute latency issue was just before I sent that message, so I suppose around that time, I checked it on my laptop when sending that message and had no issues.
But I've been having issues with load times of 30s to a few minutes for group DMs specifically in the mobile app for at least a couple months.
Right now there are no delays beyond loading the server itself, though (which always takes ~5-10 seconds). I'll post here when I next notice it :)

Just to report it, this week I’ve been seeing pretty consistent ~30s load times for DMs on the iOS app, and this morning hit a multi-minute load time. These are all single-person DMs (across a few different people), and it occurs whether there are new messages or not. There’s no delay looking at the same DMs through the zulip app on my (Mac) laptop.

(This doesn’t match the original issue of group DMs in this thread exactly, but I thought still belonged here.)
Thanks for the report -- are the desktop and mobile devices on the same network?
They are, yeah :) (I should maybe also mention that loading normal topic messages is totally fine on the iOS app, it just seems to be DMs that are the issue.)

You appear to have a very large number of unread messages, which are taking >30s to read out of the index. There are potentially some things we can do to help the query planner, but your short-term fix is to find out where those are coming from. You likely have a muted channel or set of channels. You may have seen a banner pop up saying that due to a large volume of messages being muted, you may experience some performance degradation. This is ... that. :)
Huh, okay, neat! I’ve never seen that banner, but just to be clear: this means that marking a bunch of random non-DM channels/topics as “read” may improve DM loading speed? :eyes:

Yes. The query it's running is "find me the first unread in this DM" and the query planner is choosing to do that by "find me all of Thomas' unreads, and then filter to ones in this DM" which, for you, turns out to be a poor choice.

Oh, wow, I see, thanks for the insight. So maybe the 11000+ unread messages I have in #rss could be partially to blame… :sweat_smile:

And just out of curiosity, is this just a problem with the iOS app because the query planner works differently here?

No -- it's based on the shape of the request it makes. The problematic part if the request is "jump to the first unread" which the different clients decide if they're going to provide or not, based on different logic. I do see similar 1-minute long requests from the desktop app for you, as well, when it chooses to use that flag.
Ah, ok! (Maybe I just forgot about those, or was more easily distracted by something else on my screen when it took too long? :upside_down:)

Marking all #rss messages as read seems like it may have helped matters, thanks! :) (Interestingly(?) “mark all as read” offered to mark 11,000+ messages as read, and i only saw a notification for that many, but apparently it wound up marking 38,000 messages as read according to the final popup on completion)

(There are at least ~11,000 unread in #mathlib4, but it’s useful for me to see which I’ve engaged with and how many messages each topic has, so I’ll just hope that’s not too much :grinning_face_with_smiling_eyes:)
Out of curiosity, was #rss muted for you?

When I long press on the channel itself, it just gives me the option to unsubscribe. Long pressing on individual topics like recent commits to mathlib4 gives me the option to “mute”, so I assume they’re not muted yet. I tried long pressing on all the topics, but none gave me the option to unmute. (There’s a chance I missed one or two by doing it manually, but I at least checked the high-traffic “recent commits” ones.)
(Also I did have one 30-second DM load time after I messaged (after several fast ones), but all of them seem to be very quick now.)
Topics can be muted separately from channels
https://github.com/zulip/zulip-flutter/issues/347 tracks the channel mute/unmute on mobile

Muted channels show up as greyed out on mobile, without an unread count number:
Screenshot_20260430-232707.png
Ah, no, it wasn't muted, then; I saw it in color and saw the ~11,000 unread count next to it.

As far as I can see I actually have no muted channels. At one point believe I followed #rss or a topic in it then unfollowed, but I don't remember using the mute feature specifically on anything, really; I just unsubscribe or, if it's a topic I'm automatically following, unfollow.
Sure, makes sense. Most folks tend to not leave tens of thousands of unread messages in non-muted topics, but everyone's workflows are different. :)

Haha, I think there's simply too much volume (and everything interesting to me is too commingled with everything not interesting to me, on a channel level) that going through and muting is more work (or not the right move, if it's a channel I participate in) compared to just ignoring large numbers! :sweat_smile:

I must confess I have 5000+ unread messages in an unmuted #rss representing "I used to be up to date with this channel but then got behind and now just dream of the 3 hours I need to plough through checking I didn't miss any interesting commits to lean or mathlib"

Just want to mention that I still have extremely slow load times pretty frequently, since it's not really practical for me to mark all the messages in channels I participate in as "read" (e.g. #mathlib4, which has 13k unread messages). The information of "have I actually read this topic or not" is too useful to sacrifice (as I would if I were to mass-mark them as "read"), and since I actively participate it doesn't make sense to mute the channel.

But, am I doing something wrong here? Should I be using Zulip differently? How can I retain the information of whether I've read something or not while still having fast load times?

We need to find some way to reduce the load of unread messages that Zulip churns through each time.

Would you be willing to mute topics that you don't actively participate in, maybe topics that are old and no longer active? I'll acknowledge this could take a bit of time going through various topic lists in front of your computer, but I know you don't want to mute whole channels.

Muting preserves your read/unread state accurately, allows you to still search in those topics and read them without unmuting, and you'll still be notified about @-mentions. https://zulip.com/help/mute-a-topic

The unread topics I would be muting have on the order of 1 to 100 messages, so I think I would be doing that for quite a while to reach 13k! :sweat_smile: I feel as though in net, I might save more time by just waiting each time I open the app than by going through all of those topics...I realize this means I'm probably "holding it wrong", but ultimately I'm just not willing to take the time to do that. :)

It sounds like a mostly reasonable solution if I were, though. Am I understanding correctly that for inactive topics, muted topics are indistinguishable from unmuted topics?

There are a lot of topics that have not been active in a very long time, so I wonder if topics could be effectively automuted after a while of inactivity, then…auto-unmuted if there’s ever activity? (I don’t know how anything works on the backend!)

Hmmmm, there is a time at which messages become old enough to not be included in what Zulip is caching anymore... But, I don't personally know what that threshold is. :sweat_smile: I've invited Zulip engineers to stop by and help us out here.
